verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this finding are in same-day pre-print wire copy, and the causal half is also wrong. (a) Causation: the +12.83% on 2026-08-27 (339.31 -> 382.85, verified) was NOT 'nothing but a StreetInsider rumour'. CrowdStrike reported after the close on 2026-08-26, beat and raised on AI-threat-driven demand; on 08-27 CRWD had its best day ever (+20%) and Okta +29%, and CNBC's sector piece explicitly lists 'Palo Alto Networks, SailPoint, Zscaler and Rubrik up at least 10% each' on that rally. The Cribl/ClickHouse item was a co-driver at most, and the Motley Fool retail explainer the hunter cites is the weakest available source on attribution. (b) Even taking the momentum-premium framing at face value, the premium has already come out INSIDE the sealed baseline: Aug 31 close 382.13 vs baseline spot 363.995 at 14:07 UTC = -4.7% today, and the Fool's own 2026-09-01 piece attributes today's -4.9% to pre-earnings profit-taking on a doubled EV/EBITDA multiple. (c) The reaction-function half is verified but published. I confirmed the price facts independently (Yahoo daily bars: 2025-07-28 204.50 -> 07-30 183.03 = -10.5% two-day, -> 07-31 173.60 = -15.1% three-day, so '-14% over two days' is loose but the substance holds; 2025-11-19 199.90 -> 11-20 185.07 = -7.42% exactly; 2026-02-17 163.50 -> 02-18 152.35 = -6.82% exactly). But Investing.com, published 2026-09-01 BEFORE this print, states 'Four consecutive beats. Three consecutive sell-offs', average post-earnings move ~-5.2%, range -6.67% to -8.75%, AND 'PANW surged +10.39% on August 27 - just days before earnings. The stock has already moved as if it beat.' That is this finding, both legs, in today's preview copy. The finding also omits the fourth data point (the 2026-06-02 Q3 print, ~-8.5%), which the published pattern includes. On the skew: I rule that the -17.1 call-bid skew here is NOT the market dismissing a known selloff pattern - the pattern is in today's copy and analysts still sit 41-of-54 Strong Buy - it is the market paying for a genuine two-sided AI-security demand upcycle validated 96 hours ago by CRWD and OKTA. Cheap puts here are cheap because the sector tape turned, not because a risk went unread.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline itself contains the unwind the finding wants to sell: spot 363.995 at 14:07 UTC against an 08-31 close of 382.13 is -4.7% already realised today, and run_up_5d_pct is only +3.73% versus the +12.83% single session the finding points at - i.e. roughly two-thirds of that session is already out of the tape at the seal. Skew -17.1 with calls bid and put/call OI 1.19 means downside is cheap, but I read that as the market repricing sector demand after CRWD/OKTA rather than as a dismissed risk. history.n=0 is a records bug, so the baseline states no reaction base rate - that is the one respect in which this finding adds something the pipeline did not have, and it is why this is 85 and not 95.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the 08-27 move could be shown to be idiosyncratic to PANW rather than sector-wide - e.g. PANW's 12.83% materially exceeded a cap-weighted cyber basket that day after controlling for CRWD/OKTA - the rumour-premium leg would regain force and this drops toward 55.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I accept every fact here - I checked each one against the company's own releases and they are exactly right - and reject the novelty. Verified: Q3 FY26 release (SEC-filed, 2026-06-02) guides FY26 diluted non-GAAP EPS $3.77-$3.79 on 763-766m shares and Q4 FY26 $0.96-$0.98 on 830-840m shares; Q2 FY26 release (2026-02-17) guided FY26 to $3.65-$3.70 on 768-773m, down from the Q1 FY26 release (2025-11-19) $3.80-$3.90 on 710-716m; and the 2026-02-18 reaction was -6.82% (163.50 -> 152.35). So the arithmetic is clean and the ~9-13% FY27 share-count step-up is real. But every input is in a filed 8-K exhibit that has been public for three months, and the implication is already in consensus: FY27 consensus EPS is $3.98 against FY26 guidance of $3.77-$3.79 - only +5% EPS growth against consensus FY27 revenue of $13.8bn, i.e. +21%. That 16-point wedge IS the dilution plus deal financing; sell-side has modelled it. The 112m shares issued to CyberArk holders and a '13.5% dilution of existing EPS' have been published since the 2025-07-30 announcement. Two further problems with sign and size. First, the mechanism the finding treats as a one-way ratchet already reversed once: on 2026-06-02 PANW raised FY26 EPS back to $3.77-$3.79 on a LOWER full-year share count (763-766 vs 768-773), so the Feb cut was not a durable dilution story. Second, and more important, EPS is demonstrably not this stock's decision variable. PANW went from 141.67 (2026-02-24) to a 52-week high near 396 - roughly 2.8x - across the same period its FY26 EPS guide was being cut, and every pre-print preview I found says the number that decides tonight is the initial FY27 NGS ARR guide against a FactSet-implied ~22% / $10.9bn bar, not the EPS line. On the brief's consensus-equals-guidance test: it is true (Q4 consensus $0.98 on $3.35bn vs guide $0.96-$0.98 on $3.345-3.355bn) but it is also the ordinary state of a guidance-anchored name and is itself published in today's Investing.com preview, so it does not make the FY27 guide unanchored - the FY27 anchor is public and numeric.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Nothing in the baseline is inconsistent with this being priced. Realised 20d vol of 63% and an event-implied move of 7.77% say the market expects a large print, and calls are bid (-17.1 skew), which is the opposite of a chain worried about an EPS-guide shortfall. The 2026-02-18 -6.82% reaction the finding invokes is real but happened at a $163 spot with an ARR/RPO deceleration alongside it; the stock has since risen 2.2x through further dilution, which is direct price evidence that the market prices ARR and discounts EPS optics.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If FY27 consensus EPS could be shown to be built on a share count materially below ~840m - say 800-820m, implying sell-side has not carried the Q4 exit count forward - the headline-miss risk would be genuinely unpriced and this drops toward 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I accept the fact and reject the sign. The fact is precisely stated and I verified every element against the GSA release itself (URL path ...onegov-12042025, body dated 2025-12-04): 60% off list on designated bundles of Prisma AIRS Runtime Security and VM-Series software firewalls including Panorama and Cloud Delivered Security Services; 60% on Prisma Access Enterprise (SASE and Prisma Browser); 35% on CNAPP / Code to Cloud; available through 2028-01-31. And the calendar claim holds: PANW's fiscal Q1 FY27 runs 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31, contains the 2026-09-30 federal year-end, and is the first such quarter under pricing that only began 2025-12-04. That is careful work. The problem is direction. (i) These are discounts off LIST, and PANW's realised federal pricing already ran at large discounts through GSA schedules and Carahsoft; the incremental erosion versus realised ASPs is a small fraction of 60%. (ii) OneGov is structurally a volume-for-price trade - GSA's own framing is adoption acceleration - and on subscription products a Sep-quarter federal surge lands in NGS ARR and RPO, which is exactly the metric every preview says decides tonight, not in the revenue line. (iii) The empirical test already ran: the agreement has been live across three full PANW quarters (Q2 FY26 Nov-Jan, Q3 FY26 Feb-Apr, Q4 FY26 May-Jul) and PANW raised FY26 revenue guidance in both February and June and guides Q4 NGS ARR to +59-60% - if OneGov were compressing federal economics it would already show. (iv) Size: US federal is a minority vertical for an $11.4bn revenue base; even an aggressive read on incremental discount depth is well under 1% of revenue. So the mechanism reaches the print, but I score the sign as positive-to-neutral, not negative. On publication: this sits between the 20-40 and 45-65 anchors - GSA.gov, Nextgov, MeriTalk and ExecutiveGov all carried it in December 2025, which is public but not financial press, and one equity outlet (Simply Wall St, 2025-12-14) discussed it and still framed margin pressure as coming from acquisition integration rather than federal pricing. Nine months old, on the wire, never quantified, and never linked to this print. Hence 55.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No trace of this in the baseline and none expected - the tape shows no dislocation around 2025-12-04, and the current chain (calls bid at -17.1, put/call OI 1.19) is not paying for a federal-pricing shock. I judged the cheap-put question explicitly here: puts are cheap because the sector demand signal turned positive on 2026-08-26/27, and a nine-month-old discount schedule that has already passed through three reported quarters without denting guidance is a risk the market is right to price near zero.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A PANW disclosure or 10-K line quantifying US federal as a large share of revenue together with evidence of realised ASP compression under OneGov - or management guiding Q1 FY27 revenue below consensus and naming federal pricing - would flip the sign and put this at 20.

interactions: PANW#0 and PANW#1 are not independent: both rest on the same three post-print price reactions (2025-11-20 -7.42%, 2026-02-18 -6.82%, and the 2026-06-03 ~-8.5% that #0 omits and #1 implies). Scoring both as fresh double-counts one reaction history, and that history is published in today's Investing.com preview as 'four consecutive beats, three consecutive sell-offs, average ~-5.2%'. They also partly contradict each other on mechanism: #1 treats CyberArk dilution as a one-way EPS ratchet, but the 2026-06-02 release raised FY26 EPS back to $3.77-$3.79 on a LOWER full-year share count than the February cut - so the February selloff #0 counts as a 'deal announcement' reaction and #1 counts as a 'dilution' reaction cannot both be the clean read of the same day. Third, all three findings lean negative into a chain where calls are bid, and I ruled on that once for all of them: the -17.1 skew reflects the market repricing an AI-security demand upcycle validated by CRWD (+20%, best day ever) and OKTA (+29%) on 2026-08-27, not a dismissed downside. Finally, the baseline's history.n=0 records bug is the single reason any of #0's reaction content has residual value - the pipeline has no base rate, even though the market plainly does.
